title: Accountability, Honest Reporting & Ethical Decisions
summary: Bring the unit together by applying integrity, evidence, authorization, privacy, fairness, and accountability to workplace decisions.
objectives: Evaluate workplace decisions using multiple ethical considerations.
Distinguish verified facts from unsupported claims.
Create a defensible ethical decision and explain the reasoning behind it.

vocab.def: Responsibility for actions, decisions, impacts, and appropriate follow-up.
Communicating status, results, evidence, limitations, and uncertainty accurately.
Information supported by an appropriate source or verification process.
A decision that considers evidence, policy, authorization, fairness, consequences, rights, and responsibility.

sections.heading: Ethical decisions use more than one test
sections.body: A responsible decision may require considering policy, authorization, safety, privacy, ownership, fairness, evidence, consequences, and who has authority to decide.

sections.heading: Do not turn activity into an unsupported outcome
sections.body: Completing an activity, collecting a number, or observing progress does not automatically prove a stronger outcome. Report only what the available evidence actually supports.

sections.heading: Approval must match the decision
sections.body: One approval does not automatically authorize every later use. Publishing information, making a claim, spending money, changing a record, or taking another consequential action may require separate authority.

sections.heading: Accountability continues after the decision
sections.body: Responsible workers document important decisions when required, monitor consequences, correct errors, and communicate when new information changes what should happen next.

practice.prompt: A program completed 100 lessons. Can you automatically report that 100 learners achieved career readiness?
practice.answer: No. Lesson completion and career readiness are different claims and require different evidence.

practice.prompt: A manager approved an internal draft. Does that automatically mean it may be published publicly?
practice.answer: No. Public release may require separate review and authorization.

quiz.question: Which statement best reflects ethical reporting?
options: Report only what the available evidence and authorization actually support
Turn every positive activity into an impact claim
Treat internal approval as public approval
Hide uncertainty so results appear stronger
quiz.answer: Report only what the available evidence and authorization actually support

lab.objective: Evaluate a simulated workplace decision using an ethics checklist covering evidence, authorization, privacy, ownership, fairness, consequences, uncertainty, and escalation.

reflectionPrompt: Why is an accurate smaller claim more trustworthy than a stronger claim the evidence cannot support?
